question: Among not-all-equal patterns whose knots are placed by a small automaton on binary addresses, under a description weighting: how common is each fate within level 12, and does the activity class of the relative maps change the death share at matched knot density?

public_inputs.code: written by Codex in codex/ from the spec; dlang.py's gamma and the proof note's check.py read-only
public_inputs.run: codex exec with the spec; the full run launched by the thread from Codex's runner

forbidden_inputs: Changing the spec, predictions or decision rules after seeing registered results
primary_observable: fate within level 12 per distinct pattern, by relative activity class and density bin (rho_max); weighted shares from W
cheapest_meaningful_control: matched knot density (the dull explanation); settled-by-construction descriptions excluded; both readings of undecided
validation_gate: V-act, V-rel, V-sat, V-B0, V-act-class, V-code, V-resume of the spec; any failure invalidates the run

predictions.P1: single placement and first-letter-settled descriptions are F3
predictions.P4: some unsettled exponential description first dies at level >= 9
predictions.H-bound: bounded die less than exponential at rho_max >= 1.5

stop_rule: One Codex hand-off, one full run by the thread, its summary; a referee hand-off; report.
